vocabulary.meaning_en: to talk and share news after some time apart

vocabulary.example: After the trip I was beat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the soft part in your mouth you use to talk
vocabulary.example: It's on the tip of my tongue.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small plant like a short tree
rain, sun, wind and so on

vocabulary.example: He lost his temper in the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a decision you reach after thinking
a dry stem of a plant
the area where you play some sports
vocabulary.example: The ball is in your court.
We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

fine_lines.title: catch up vs ketchup
fine_lines.explanation_ar: catch up (كاتش أب) = نتبادل الأخبار، وفيها كلمتان. ketchup (كاتشب) = الصلصة الحمراء. انطق catch up كلمتين واضحتين.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Catch up" (two words) = share news. "Ketchup" = the red sauce. Say "catch up" as two clear words.

examples.sentence: Let's meet for coffee and catch up.
Do you want ketchup with your fries?

fine_lines.title: I'm beat vs I'm under the weather
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I'm beat = أنا متعب جدًا (من العمل أو الجهد). under the weather = أشعر بتوعك أو مرض خفيف.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I'm beat" = very tired. "Under the weather" = a little sick.

examples.sentence: I worked twelve hours today. I'm beat.
I'm staying home; I'm a bit under the weather.

fine_lines.title: We'll see vs Let's play it by ear
fine_lines.explanation_ar: We'll see = سنرى (لم أقرر بعد). Let's play it by ear = لنقرر حسب الظروف في وقتها، بدون خطة مسبقة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "We'll see" = I haven't decided yet. "Play it by ear" = decide later depending on what happens.

examples.sentence: Can we go to the beach tomorrow? - We'll see.
I don't know the weather, so let's play it by ear.

expressions.meaning_en: A warm greeting when you haven't seen someone for a while.
expressions.example: Hi Nora! How have you been?

expressions.meaning_en: Asking about someone's life in general.
expressions.example: How's everything going at your new job?

expressions.meaning_en: A good answer to "How are you?"
expressions.example: How are you? - I'm doing well, thanks.

expressions.meaning_en: Said when you meet after a long time.
expressions.example: Long time no see! You look great.

expressions.phrase: What have you been up to?
expressions.meaning_en: Asking what someone has been doing lately.
expressions.example: So, what have you been up to these days?

expressions.meaning_en: Let's meet and talk again soon.
expressions.example: I have to go now, but let's catch up soon.

expressions.meaning_en: Said when you find a surprising connection.
expressions.example: You know my cousin? Small world!

expressions.meaning_en: I haven't decided yet.
expressions.example: Will you travel this summer? - We'll see.

expressions.meaning_en: I'm very tired.
expressions.example: What a long day. I'm beat.

expressions.meaning_en: I support you; I'll help you.
expressions.example: Don't worry about the presentation. I've got your back.

expressions.meaning_en: It's not a problem.
expressions.example: Sorry I'm late. - No big deal.

expressions.meaning_en: A reply to "thank you".
expressions.example: Thanks for helping me move. - Don't mention it.

expressions.meaning_en: Relax, don't be upset.
expressions.example: Calm down, we'll find your keys.

expressions.meaning_ar: أن تأتي متأخرًا خير من ألا تأتي.
expressions.meaning_en: Doing something late is better than not doing it.
expressions.example: I started learning English at forty. Better late than never!

expressions.meaning_en: I'll tell you any news.
expressions.example: I'm waiting for the results. I'll keep you posted.

expressions.meaning_en: Let's stop and rest a little.
expressions.example: We've worked for two hours. Let's take a quick break.

expressions.meaning_en: Good luck (before a show or a big event).
expressions.example: You have your speech today? Break a leg!

expressions.meaning_en: Help me.
expressions.example: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?

expressions.meaning_en: Be ready and alert.
expressions.example: The manager may visit today, so stay on your toes.

expressions.meaning_en: Don't give up; things will get better.
expressions.example: The exams are almost over. Hang in there!

expressions.meaning_en: Let's start the real work now.
expressions.example: Okay, enough small talk. Let's get down to business.

expressions.meaning_en: Wait a moment.
expressions.example: Hold on a second, I'll check.

expressions.meaning_en: I understand.
expressions.example: Send it by five. - Got it.

expressions.meaning_en: I'm going to tell you the truth.
expressions.example: To be honest with you, I don't like the new plan.

expressions.phrase: I'll be there in a bit.
expressions.meaning_en: I'll arrive soon.
expressions.example: Start without me; I'll be there in a bit.

expressions.meaning_en: It's very easy.
expressions.example: Don't worry about the test. It's a piece of cake.

expressions.phrase: It's on the tip of my tongue.
expressions.meaning_en: I almost remember it.
expressions.example: What's his name? It's on the tip of my tongue!

expressions.meaning_ar: لا تلفّ وتدور / ادخل في الموضوع.
expressions.meaning_en: Say it directly.
expressions.example: Don't beat around the bush. What happened?

expressions.meaning_en: Let's contact each other again to check progress.
expressions.example: Let's touch base next week about the project.

expressions.meaning_en: Let's decide later, not now.
expressions.example: I'm not sure about the plan. Let's play it by ear.

expressions.meaning_en: Imagine you are in my situation.
expressions.example: Put yourself in my shoes. What would you do?

expressions.meaning_en: I feel a little sick.
expressions.example: I'm feeling under the weather, so I'll stay home.

expressions.meaning_en: Very rarely.
expressions.example: We eat fast food once in a blue moon.

expressions.meaning_en: You are joking.
expressions.example: You met the president? You're pulling my leg!

expressions.meaning_en: Let's stop working for today.
expressions.example: It's six o'clock. Let's call it a day.

expressions.meaning_en: It sounds familiar.
expressions.example: Ahmed Salem? That name rings a bell.

expressions.meaning_en: I'm listening carefully.
expressions.example: Tell me your idea. I'm all ears.

expressions.phrase: I can't put my finger on it.
expressions.meaning_en: I can't say exactly what it is.
expressions.example: Something is wrong, but I can't put my finger on it.

expressions.meaning_en: We agree and understand the same thing.
expressions.example: Good, so we're on the same page about the budget.

expressions.meaning_en: I can't control it.
expressions.example: I'm sorry, the decision is out of my hands.

expressions.phrase: We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
expressions.meaning_en: We'll deal with that problem later, if it happens.
expressions.example: What if it rains? - We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

expressions.meaning_en: Let's start talking to make people relaxed.
expressions.example: Let's break the ice: everyone, say your name and your hobby.

expressions.meaning_en: Understand the hidden meaning.
expressions.example: He said he's fine, but read between the lines: he's upset.

expressions.meaning_en: The final problem that makes you lose patience.
expressions.example: He was late again. That's the last straw!

expressions.phrase: The ball is in your court.
expressions.meaning_en: Now it's your turn to decide or act.
expressions.example: I sent my offer. The ball is in your court.

expressions.meaning_en: Do something hard that you must do.
expressions.example: I hate the dentist, but I'll bite the bullet and go.

expressions.phrase: Kill two birds with one stone.
expressions.meaning_en: Do two things with one action.
expressions.example: I'll visit the bank near my school and kill two birds with one stone.

expressions.meaning_en: Become very angry.
expressions.example: Try not to lose your temper with the kids.

expressions.meaning_en: Don't decide before you know all the facts.
expressions.example: He isn't answering? Don't jump to conclusions; maybe he's busy.

grammar.title: Present perfect in greetings: How have you been?
grammar.explanation_ar: How have you been? وWhat have you been up to? تستخدمان have + been لأننا نسأل عن الفترة من آخر لقاء حتى الآن.
grammar.explanation_en: "How have you been?" and "What have you been up to?" use have + been because we ask about the time from our last meeting until now.
examples: What have you been up to?

grammar.title: Let's + verb in idioms
grammar.explanation_ar: كثير من التعابير تبدأ بـ Let's + فعل أصلي لاقتراح شيء معًا: Let's call it a day، Let's touch base.
grammar.explanation_en: Many idioms start with "Let's + base verb" to suggest something together.

grammar.title: Idioms: the meaning is not the words
grammar.explanation_ar: التعبير الاصطلاحي (idiom) معناه ليس مجموع كلماته. a piece of cake لا تعني قطعة كعك بل سهل جدًا. احفظ التعبير كاملًا مع معناه ومثاله.
grammar.explanation_en: An idiom's meaning is not the meaning of its words. "A piece of cake" means very easy. Learn the whole idiom with an example.
examples: It's a piece of cake. = It's very easy.
The ball is in your court. = It's your decision now.
I'm under the weather. = I feel a little sick.

questions.question: "It's a piece of cake" means:
questions.explanation_ar: a piece of cake = سهل جدًا.

questions.question: You almost remember a name but can't say it. You say:
choices: It's on the tip of my tongue.
questions.explanation_ar: on the tip of my tongue = على طرف لساني.

questions.question: Your friend wants to say "Let's meet and share news." Which is correct?
questions.explanation_ar: catch up = نتبادل الأخبار، وليست ketchup.

questions.question: Someone says "Thank you!" You reply:
questions.explanation_ar: Don't mention it = لا شكر على واجب.

questions.question: "Once in a blue moon" means:
questions.explanation_ar: once in a blue moon = نادرًا جدًا.

questions.question: It's 6 p.m. and everyone is tired. The manager says:
questions.explanation_ar: call it a day = ننهي العمل لهذا اليوم.
questions.explanation_en: "Call it a day" means stop work for today.

questions.question: "Don't beat around the bush" means:
questions.explanation_ar: beat around the bush = يلف ويدور، فالمعنى: تكلم مباشرة.

questions.question: Choose the correct greeting for a friend you haven't seen for months.
questions.explanation_ar: الصيغة الصحيحة: How have you been?
questions.explanation_en: The correct form is "How have you been?"

questions.question: "The ball is in your court" means:
questions.explanation_ar: the ball is in your court = القرار الآن لك.
questions.explanation_en: It means it's your decision now.
